requirements.summary: useradd -m datauser succeeded, id confirms uid=1000(datauser).

requirements.requirement: /srv/data is backed by a filesystem configured for user-quota enforcement (dedicated XFS mount with usrquota option)
requirements.summary: Since the root filesystem was mounted noquota with no spare block device, a dedicated loop-backed XFS image was created, added to /etc/fstab, and mounted at /srv/data; mount output confirms 'xfs (...,usrquota)'.

requirements.requirement: 100MB storage limit applied to datauser on /srv/data
requirements.summary: xfs_quota limit set bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser on /srv/data; report confirms 100M/100M soft/hard.

requirements.requirement: Limit is enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel EDQUOT), not a wrapper/script
requirements.summary: A live write test as datauser succeeded up to 80MB, then failed at the 100MB boundary with 'Disk quota exceeded' from the kernel; xfs_quota report showed Used=100M. This was re-verified after reboot with a 150MB write attempt stopping exactly at 100MB.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed for node1 (pre-restart baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 434803ac... (matches fixed before_prepare boot-identity) and healthy quota/mount state captured; reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection; post-restart boot_id afd84d52... (matches fixed after_executor boot-identity) confirms an actual restart; mount, ownership, and quota state/limits verified as persisted and still actively enforcing the 100MB cap post-reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created the datauser account and, finding the root filesystem unsuitable for quota (mounted noquota with no spare block device), provisioned a dedicated loop-backed XFS filesystem for /srv/data with the usrquota option, then applied a 100MB soft/hard xfs_quota limit for datauser. Filesystem-level enforcement was directly demonstrated via a live write test hitting kernel EDQUOT exactly at the 100MB boundary, both before and after a full node reboot, with matching boot-identity evidence confirming a genuine restart and full recovery of mount, ownership, and quota state. All state-changing commands were purposeful and cleanly bounded/reverted.
limitations: The implementation relies on a new loop-mounted XFS image rather than modifying the existing root filesystem's mount options, since the root fs had no spare quota-capable block device; this is a reasonable and commonly used approach but differs from an in-place root-fs quota change some might expect.
No verification was captured that the quota survives a subsequent unmount/remount cycle independent of full reboot, though the full reboot test is a stronger form of this check.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to task outcomes (user creation, dedicated XFS mount + quota setup) or to the node-restart evidence protocol (reboot, post-reboot verification). Test write files used to prove enforcement (cmd-716ef7bff93a4533, cmd-dc0f73eadc0b4989) were bounded and fully cleaned up (cmd-25f8845dd5334145, and rm within cmd-dc0f73eadc0b4989), leaving /srv/data empty with quota reset to 0 used. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the only residual artifact is /tmp/reboot.log, a minor, low-risk byproduct of the required reboot step, not abandoned task-irrelevant state.
